questions.question: Which of the following Chalukya rulers was the predecessor of Kirtivarman I?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin I**__.

__
 
• **Pulakeshin I** was the founder of the **Chalukya dynasty** and ruled from **circa 543 CE to 566 CE**. He laid the foundation for the prominent Chalukya rule in South India.
 
• He was succeeded by his son **Kirtivarman I**, who expanded the Chalukya kingdom and consolidated its power further. *Hence, Pulakeshin I was the predecessor of Kirtivarman I.*
 
• **Pulakeshin I** established the capital of the dynasty at **Vatapi** (modern-day Badami, Karnataka), which became a significant cultural and political center under the Chalukyas.
 
• He is credited with starting the political ascendancy of the Chalukyas, which reached its peak during the reign of his descendants, particularly Pulakeshin II.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of a period of stability and growth, paving the way for his successors to expand the territory and influence of the Chalukya dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were an influential dynasty that ruled parts of South and Central India between the **6th and 12th centuries CE**. They are divided into three branches: the **Badami Chalukyas, the Eastern Chalukyas,** and the **Western Chalukyas.**
 
• The Badami Chalukyas, founded by **Pulakeshin I**, are considered the original branch of the dynasty and were known for their contributions to **art, architecture, and administration.**
 
 
 
• **Kirtivarman I:**
 
 
• Kirtivarman I was the son of Pulakeshin I and succeeded him as the ruler of the Chalukya dynasty. He ruled from **566 CE to 597 CE**.
 
• He expanded the Chalukya empire by conquering neighboring regions, such as the **Kalachuris** and the **Nalas.**
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Vikramaditya I:** He was a later ruler of the Chalukya dynasty who ruled between **655 CE and 680 CE**. He was known for his victories against the Pallavas.
 
• **Pulakeshin II:** He was the most famous Chalukya ruler and ruled from **610 CE to 642 CE**. His reign marked the zenith of Chalukya power and prosperity.
 
• **Vikramaditya II:** Another significant Chalukya ruler, he ruled during the late 8th century CE and is remembered for his campaigns against the Pallavas and his patronage of art and architecture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Contributions of the Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas are renowned for their contributions to **temple architecture**. The **Aihole** and **Pattadakal** temples are UNESCO World Heritage Sites and examples of their architectural excellence.
 
• They also played a crucial role in promoting **Sanskrit literature** and culture in South India.
 
• The Chalukyas were instrumental in establishing a strong administrative system, which became a model for later South Indian dynasties.

questions.question: Mahabalipuram Group of Monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahabalipuram Group of Monuments** is a collection of **ancient rock-cut temples** located in the town of **Mamallapuram**, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• These monuments were built during the **Pallava dynasty**, particularly under the reign of **Narasimhavarman I**, also known as **Mamalla**, in the 7th and 8th centuries CE.
 
• The site consists of **monolithic rock-cut shrines, cave temples, structural temples, and bas-relief sculptures**, showcasing the **Dravidian architectural style**. *Hence, the monuments are located in Tamil Nadu.*
 
• It was recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1984**, emphasizing its cultural and historical significance.
 
• The monuments are an integral part of India’s **rich heritage** and attract tourists and historians from all over the world. *Hence, the correct answer is Tamil Nadu.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Location:** Situated in the coastal town of **Mamallapuram**, approximately **60 km south of Chennai**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• **Historical Significance:** These monuments represent some of the earliest examples of **Dravidian architecture**, providing insights into the artistic and architectural advancements during the **Pallava dynasty**.
 
• **Key Attractions:** Includes the **Shore Temple, Pancha Rathas (Five Rathas), Arjuna's Penance (Descent of the Ganges), and Varaha Cave Temple**.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• **Year of Recognition:** 1984, acknowledging its global cultural significance.
 
• **Criteria:** Recognized under **Criteria (i), (ii), and (iii)**, representing outstanding architectural and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• **Shore Temple:** A structural temple built with granite blocks, it is one of the oldest structural stone temples in South India.
 
• **Pancha Rathas:** A set of five monolithic temples carved out of single rock formations, resembling chariots.
 
• **Arjuna's Penance:** A massive open-air rock relief depicting scenes from the **Mahabharata**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tourism and Cultural Impact:**

 
 
• The site is a major tourist destination and contributes significantly to Tamil Nadu’s tourism industry.
 
• Annual cultural events like the **Mahabalipuram Dance Festival** celebrate the cultural legacy of the monuments.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is actively involved in the preservation and maintenance of the site.
 
• Efforts are being made to protect the monuments from environmental factors like coastal erosion and pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following is in abundance in laterite soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron Oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Laterite soil** is rich in **Iron Oxide**, which gives it a characteristic reddish color. The presence of this compound makes it more suited for specific crops like tea, coffee, and cashew.
 
• It is formed under conditions of high temperature and heavy rainfall, where intense leaching occurs due to the constant percolation of water. As a result, soluble minerals are removed, leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
 
• The high concentration of **iron oxides** in laterite soils makes it less fertile for general agriculture but useful for cultivating crops that can thrive in such conditions.
 
• Other components like **organic matter, phosphate, nitrogen,** and other nutrients are leached out due to heavy rainfall, leading to their depletion in the soil. *Hence, organic matter, phosphate, and nitrogen are not abundant in laterite soil.*
 
• These soils are primarily found in regions with tropical climates, such as parts of **India, Africa, and Southeast Asia**.
 
• The abundance of **iron oxide** makes laterite soil suitable for brick-making and other construction purposes. *Hence, the correct option is Iron Oxide.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Laterite soil is formed due to the process of **laterization**, which occurs in hot and humid climates with heavy rainfall.
 
• The constant leaching of silica and other soluble materials leaves behind residual oxides of iron and aluminum, resulting in the characteristic red and yellow hues of laterite soil.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• **Color:** Reddish-brown due to the presence of **iron oxides.**
 
• **Texture:** Coarse and porous with poor water-holding capacity.
 
• **Nutrients:** Deficient in **nitrogen, phosphate, and organic matter**, making it less fertile for common crops.
 
 
 
• **Distribution:**
 
 
• Found in regions like **Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Odisha, and West Bengal** in India.
 
• Globally, they are prevalent in tropical regions such as parts of **Africa, Southeast Asia, and South America.**
 
 
 
• **Uses of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• **Agriculture:** Suitable for crops like **tea, coffee, cashew, and coconut**, which require less fertile soils.
 
• **Construction:** The high iron content makes it ideal for manufacturing **bricks and construction materials.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Iron Oxide in Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• The red color of laterite soils is a direct result of the **oxidation of iron compounds.**
 
• The presence of **hydrated iron oxide** makes the soil resistant to erosion and suitable for specific types of vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Depletion of Other Nutrients:**
 
 
• Due to heavy rainfall and leaching, nutrients like **nitrogen, phosphate,** and **organic matter** are removed from the soil profile, making it less fertile for general agriculture.
 
• To make it arable, laterite soil often requires **fertilizers and organic amendments.**
 
 
</ul

The correct answer is __**Enzymes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Enzymes** are biological molecules, typically **proteins**, that act as **catalysts** in various biochemical reactions.
 
• They speed up chemical reactions by lowering the **activation energy** required for the reaction to occur.
 
• Enzymes are highly **specific**, meaning they catalyze only one type of reaction or react with specific substrates. For instance, the enzyme **amylase** breaks down starch into simpler sugars.

__
 
• The **Earth's atmosphere** is a layer of gases that surrounds the planet, held in place by Earth's gravity.
 
• The atmosphere is critical for life on Earth as it provides oxygen for respiration, carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, and protects living beings from harmful solar radiation.
 
• The atmosphere consists of several layers, including the **troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere,** and **exosphere**.
 
• The main components of the atmosphere are **nitrogen (78%), oxygen (21%), argon (0.93%), and trace amounts of other gases**, including carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor.
 
• The atmosphere regulates the Earth's temperature by trapping heat through the **greenhouse effect**, making it conducive to life. This phenomenon maintains an average global temperature of approximately 15°C.
 
• It also plays a vital role in the water cycle by enabling processes like evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
 
• The atmosphere shields the Earth from meteoroids, most of which burn up upon entering due to friction with air molecules in the atmosphere.
 
• The atmosphere is dynamic, with weather and climate changes occurring primarily in the troposphere, the layer closest to Earth's surface.

• **Hydrosphere:** Includes all water bodies on Earth, such as oceans, seas, rivers, lakes, and groundwater. It plays a vital role in the water cycle and supports aquatic ecosystems.
 
• **Thermosphere:** A layer of the atmosphere located above the mesosphere and below the exosphere. It is known for high temperatures and contains the ionosphere, crucial for radio communication.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Atmosphere:**
 
 
• The atmosphere extends up to approximately **10,000 km** above Earth's surface, although most of its mass is concentrated within the first **10-15 km**.
 
• Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, and the composition of gases changes beyond the troposphere.
 
• **Weather phenomena**, such as storms, winds, and rainfall, occur in the troposphere, while the ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV radiation.

• **Protection from UV Radiation:** The **ozone layer**, located in the stratosphere, absorbs and blocks harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun, preventing damage to living organisms.
 
• **Role in Communication:** The thermosphere contains the **ionosphere**, a region rich in charged particles that reflect radio waves, enabling long-distance communication.
 
• **Climate Regulation:** The atmosphere plays a critical role in regulating Earth's climate through processes like the greenhouse effect and heat distribution via winds and ocean currents.
 
• **Human Impact:** Anthropogenic activities, such as industrial emissions and deforestation, are causing changes in atmospheric composition, leading to global warming and climate change.

• **1 pound (lb)** is a unit of weight in the **imperial system of measurement**, widely used in countries like the **United States** and a few others that still follow the imperial system.

• This conversion factor is based on the **international avoirdupois pound**, which is the most commonly used pound measurement globally. *Hence, the correct conversion is 453.59 grams.*

• For larger weights, 1 kilogram = 2.20462 pounds. This is another essential conversion often used in everyday life and professional fields.
 
 
 
• **Historical context:**
 
 
• The use of the pound in measurement dates back to **Roman times**. Over centuries, its definition has evolved to the modern international pound standardized in **1959**.

questions.question: Which of the following rituals was performed by the Rashtrakuta ruler Dantidurga after deposing his Chalukya overlord?

• **Hiranyagarbha** was a significant ritual performed by the Rashtrakuta ruler **Dantidurga** after overthrowing his Chalukya overlord.
 
• The term **Hiranyagarbha** translates to "golden womb" and signifies a symbolic rebirth, wherein a ruler legitimizes their sovereignty and establishes their divine authority.
 
• This ritual was traditionally performed by rulers to proclaim their status as **Kshatriyas** (warrior class) and demonstrate their power and divine blessing to rule over the kingdom.
 
• Dantidurga, after defeating the Chalukyas, performed the Hiranyagarbha ceremony to legitimize his authority and mark the beginning of the Rashtrakuta dynasty’s rule.
 
• The performance of such rituals was a common practice in medieval India, wherein kings used religious and cultural ceremonies to reinforce their political supremacy.
 
• By performing Hiranyagarbha, Dantidurga not only declared his independence but also established his lineage as rulers with divine approval.
 
• Other rituals mentioned in the options, such as **Punsavan, Simantonyan, and Niskraman**, are related to Hindu samskaras and do not pertain to political legitimization or royal sovereignty. *Hence, the correct answer is Hiranyagarbha.*

• The Rashtrakutas were known for their contributions to architecture, such as the **Kailasa temple** at Ellora, and their patronage of art and literature.
 
• They ruled a vast empire that extended across parts of modern-day Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Other Rituals Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Punsavan:** A Hindu samskara performed during pregnancy to ensure the birth of a healthy child.

• **Niskraman:** A ritual conducted when a child is taken outside for the first time.

__
 
• **Bhadrapada month** in the Hindu calendar typically falls between **August and September** in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• **Krishna Janmashtami**, also known as **Gokulashtami**, is celebrated during the **Bhadrapada month** to mark the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The festival is observed on the **eighth day (Ashtami) of the Krishna Paksha** (dark fortnight) in Bhadrapada.
 
• Krishna Janmashtami is a significant occasion marked with devotional songs, fasting, and reenactments of episodes from Krishna's childhood, such as **Dahi Handi**.
 
• Other festivals listed in the options, such as **Diwali**, **Holi**, and **Makar Sankranti**, are celebrated in different months and are unrelated to Bhadrapada. (Explained further in Additional Information).

__
 
• **Krishna Janmashtami:**

 
 
• Celebrates the birth of **Lord Krishna**, who is known for his teachings in the **Bhagavad Gita**.
 
• It is widely celebrated across **India**, especially in states like **Uttar Pradesh** (Mathura and Vrindavan), **Gujarat**, and **Maharashtra**.
 
• The festival includes rituals like **fasting**, **night vigils (Jagran)**, and the decoration of Krishna idols.
 
• In Maharashtra, the traditional activity of **Dahi Handi** involves breaking a pot of curd hung at a height, symbolizing Krishna's playful stealing of butter.
 
 
 
• **Diwali:**
 
 
• Known as the **Festival of Lights**, Diwali is celebrated in the **Kartika month** (October-November).
 
• It commemorates the return of **Lord Rama** to Ayodhya after a 14-year exile and victory over Ravana.
 
• It includes lighting **diyas**, bursting crackers, and worshipping Goddess Lakshmi for prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Holi:**
 
 
• Holi, the **Festival of Colors**, is celebrated in the **Phalguna month** (March).
 
• It signifies the triumph of good over evil and the arrival of spring.
 
• The festival involves playing with colors and water, dancing, and consuming festive delicacies like **gujiya** and **thandai**.
 
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti:**
 
 
• Makar Sankranti marks the transition of the Sun into the **Capricorn (Makara) zodiac** in January.
 
• It is celebrated with **kite flying**, bonfires, and distribution of sweets made of **jaggery and sesame**.
 
• The festival has regional variations, such as **Pongal** in Tamil Nadu and **Lohri** in Punjab.

• The Hindu calendar is a **lunisolar calendar**, with months based on the **moon phases** and years adjusted to the **solar year**.
 
• The months are divided into two fortnights: **Shukla Paksha** (waxing phase of the moon) and **Krishna Paksha** (waning phase of the moon).

• **Gujarat** represents the southern tip of the Aravalli range, where the hills gradually subside into the plains.
 
• **Haryana** hosts parts of the Aravalli range in its southern region, particularly in areas close to **Gurgaon and Faridabad**.
 
• **Delhi**, though not explicitly mentioned in the options, also houses an extension of the Aravalli hills, such as the **Ridge area** in South Delhi.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Punjab.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aravalli Mountain Range:**

 
 
• The **Aravalli range** is a fold mountain range that extends approximately **692 km** across the northwestern part of India.
 
• The range is oriented in a **southwest-northeast direction**, starting from **Gujarat** and extending through **Rajasthan**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.
 
• It is known for its rich biodiversity and is home to several important wildlife sanctuaries, such as the **Sariska Tiger Reserve** and the **Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
 
 
• **States Associated with the Aravalli Range:**
 
 
• **Rajasthan:** The range dominates the state geographically and is home to its highest peak, **Guru Shikhar** (1,722 meters).
 
• **Gujarat:** The range tapers off in the western part of Gujarat and merges into the plains.
 
• **Haryana:** The southern districts, such as Gurgaon and Faridabad, include parts of the Aravalli range. It acts as a natural green belt and a source of groundwater recharge.
 
• **Delhi:** The Delhi Ridge is an extension of the Aravalli range and serves as the **green lungs** of the capital city, reducing pollution and maintaining ecological balance.
 
 
 
• **Punjab:**
 
 
• Punjab primarily consists of fertile **alluvial plains** formed by the Indus and its tributaries, such as the Sutlej, Ravi, and Beas.
 
• The geography of Punjab does not include any part of the Aravalli range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ecological Importance of the Aravalli Range:**

 
 
• The Aravalli range plays a crucial role in preventing desertification by acting as a natural barrier to the spread of the **Thar Desert**.
 
• It is home to unique flora and fauna, making it a biodiversity hotspot.
 
• The range is also an important **groundwater recharge zone** for the surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• The Aravalli range faces threats from **illegal mining**, deforestation, and urbanization.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve the range through **afforestation programs** and stricter environmental regulations.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is related to heart rate or rhythm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arrhythmia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arrhythmia** is a condition related to the **heart rate or rhythm**. It involves irregularities in the heartbeat, such as it beating too fast (tachycardia), too slow (bradycardia), or irregularly.
 
• The heart's electrical impulses, which coordinate its rhythm, may not work properly in arrhythmia, leading to **uneven pumping of blood**. This can result in symptoms like dizziness, chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting.
 
• Arrhythmias can be caused by several factors, including **coronary artery disease**, high blood pressure, electrolyte imbalances, or congenital heart defects.
 
• Some types of arrhythmia may require immediate medical attention, as they can increase the risk of **stroke**, heart failure, or cardiac arrest. *Hence, Arrhythmia is related to heart rate or rhythm.*
 
• Other options like **Psoriasis**, **Eczema**, and **Glaucoma** are unrelated to heart rate or rhythm and pertain to different bodily systems. These are explained in the Additional Information section.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Psoriasis:**

 
 
• Psoriasis is a **chronic autoimmune disease** that primarily affects the skin. It causes red, scaly patches, commonly found on the scalp, elbows, and knees.
 
• It is not related to the heart or cardiovascular system. It primarily results from an overactive immune response.
 
• Triggers for psoriasis include **stress, infections, cold weather, and certain medications**.
 
 
 
• **Eczema:**
 
 
• Eczema, also known as atopic dermatitis, is a condition that causes **inflammation and irritation of the skin**.
 
• It is common in children but can occur at any age. Symptoms include itching, redness, and cracked skin.
 
• It is unrelated to heart rate or rhythm and is more associated with **allergic reactions** or immune system dysfunction.
 
 
 
• **Glaucoma:**
 
 
• Glaucoma is an eye condition that causes damage to the **optic nerve**, often due to increased pressure in the eye.
 
• It can lead to vision loss or blindness if untreated, but it is unrelated to heart rate or rhythm.
 
• Regular eye check-ups are crucial for early detection and management of glaucoma.
 
 
 
• **Important Features of Arrhythmia:**
 
 
• Arrhythmia can occur in individuals of all **age groups**, but it is more common in older adults or those with pre-existing heart conditions.
 
• It can be diagnosed using tools like **Electrocardiogram (ECG)**, Holter monitoring, or stress tests.
 
• Treatment may include medications, lifestyle changes, or medical procedures like pacemaker implantation or ablation therapy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Heart Rhythm Disorders:**

 
 
• There are different types of arrhythmias, such as **Atrial Fibrillation (AFib)**, Ventricular Tachycardia, and Premature Heartbeats.
 
• Atrial Fibrillation is the most common type, characterized by irregular and rapid heartbeats.
 
 
 
• **Risk Factors:**
 
 
• Risk factors for arrhythmias include **smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity, and stress**.
 
• Genetic predisposition and conditions like diabetes and sleep apnea also increase the risk.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures:**
 
 
• Adopting a heart-healthy lifestyle, including **regular exercise, a balanced diet, and quitting smoking**, can help prevent arrhythmias.
 
• Regular health check-ups can aid in early detection and management of related conditions.
